newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter sees layoffs in equity unit -- sources.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter sees layoffs in equity unit -- sources.

text.p: Substantial layoffs at Dean Witter, Discover and Co., are expected as a result of the brokerage company's $10.7 billion merger with Morgan Stanley Group Inc., sources said Friday.
The layoffs are likely to occur in divisions that handle retail customer business in stocks, stock market research and trading, said the sources, who spoke on condition of not being named.

Dean Witter sources said equity traders and the institutional sales force were told by Bob Sculthorpe, executive vice president of the equity division, in a meeting on Thursday there would likely be layoffs in the department.
No details were given at the meeting.
Sculthorpe was not immediately available for comment and a Dean Witter spokesman had no immediate comment.
The sources said traders and salesmen would likely be informed next week of layoffs. The sources said a similar meeting was held on Wednesday for equity research analysts.
Senior executives of both companies were meeting Friday to map out details of what personnel they would need, the sources said.
One employee in the Dean Witter equity unit said workers were expecting to remain at the firm for about six months until the deal was finalised, but workers there expected widespread layoffs.
Talk of layoffs follows the announcement Wednesday that the two companies agreed to merge, creating the nation's largest brokerage.
Morgan Stanley was up 62.5 cents at $67 and Dean Witter was was up 37.5 cents a $41.375, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
